title: The componentwise product of left exact functors on a finite product of abelian categories is left exact
statement: Let $I$ be a finite set and, for each $i\in I$, let $\mathcal A_i$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] and $\Gamma_i:\mathcal A_i\to\mathbf{Ab}$ an additive left exact functor [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. In the product category $\prod_{i\in I}\mathcal A_i$ (objects families $(A_i)_i$, morphisms families $(f_i)_i$) finite biproducts and kernels exist and are computed componentwise, and the functor $\Gamma:\prod_{i\in I}\mathcal A_i\to\mathbf{Ab}$, $\Gamma((A_i)_i)=\prod_{i\in I}\Gamma_i(A_i)$, $\Gamma((f_i)_i)=\prod_{i\in I}\Gamma_i(f_i)$, is additive and left exact.

source.place: Homology, Lemma 060K (homology-lemma-product-abelian-groups-exact, homology.tex line 7921: products of exact sequences of abelian groups are exact) together with the componentwise structure of a product category; formulation supplied by the reviewer

proof.text: The product category has a zero object and finite biproducts by taking the corresponding objects and maps in each component. For a morphism family $(f_i)_i$, its kernel is the family of componentwise kernels, since a cone into this family is a cone into each $\ker(f_i)$ and the componentwise universal properties assemble into the universal property in the product category. Thus the finite biproduct and kernel assertions hold.

source.place: Homology, Lemma 060K (homology-lemma-product-abelian-groups-exact), together with the componentwise universal properties of finite biproducts and kernels in a product category

proof.text: For each $i$, additivity of $\Gamma_i$ identifies its value on a finite biproduct with the corresponding product in $\mathbf{Ab}$, and left exactness identifies its value on a componentwise kernel with the kernel of the induced map. The finite product in $\mathbf{Ab}$ is a finite biproduct, so the componentwise formula $\Gamma((A_i)_i)=\prod_i\Gamma_i(A_i)$ preserves finite products and carries the componentwise kernel to the kernel of $\Gamma((f_i)_i)$. By the definition of an additive left exact functor, $\Gamma$ is additive and left exact.
